deferredCommits.reason: Media Foundation control-flow and test prerequisites diverge from the pinned CrossOver branch.
CrossOver carries a divergent WinHTTP stream implementation and the upstream commit adds no in-tree regression test.
The source hunk applies but the matching SChannel test prerequisite does not; source-only backporting is not accepted.
The implementation moved from setupapi to cfgmgr32 upstream; this requires semantic adaptation and a matching legacy-layout test.
The URI safety fix depends on the surrounding canonicalization series and must be evaluated as an ordered chain.
The ucrtbase test prerequisite rewrites unrelated test_cexp and test_expf assertions whose outcome depends on 11.x math fixes absent from the pinned base; source-only backporting is not accepted.
Switching UnhandledExceptionFilter from the PEB BeingDebugged flag to the debug port changes the crash path for titles that tamper with that flag and needs product evidence first.

Upstream converted the monitor DPI helpers to fractional ratios after 11.0, so the detached-source guard needs a hand-written adaptation in abi-sensitive display code with no upstream regression test.
Rectifying the pixel aspect ratio adds new output behaviour rather than fixing a defect, and no Runeon title is known to need it.
The fix targets the batched raw mouse input mechanism introduced after 11.0; the base has no info->raw_mouse path to repair.
WINHTTP_OPTION_SERVER_CERT_CHAIN_CONTEXT does not exist in the pinned base; the fix requires porting the whole option first.
Same missing WINHTTP_OPTION_SERVER_CERT_CHAIN_CONTEXT prerequisite as f27d14a21cfe.
pGetWindowStateUpdates is implemented only by winex11.drv; the host window state race the lock protects against does not exist on the macOS driver.
Planar CPU blits belong to the wined3d Vulkan H.264 decoder chain, which Runeon does not use because video decoding runs through D3DMetal and DXVK.
The bound check it removes was added by 2e68942fce46 inside the same release window and never reached the pinned base, so the pair is a no-op here.

A complete i386/x86_64 WoW64 build is still required before tagging; the original application crash has not been reproduced locally.

patches.adaptation: Upstream moves wglCreateContextAttribsARB parsing into win32u as part of an OpenGL context refactor that the 11.19 sweep did not take. This patch carries only the resulting winemac.drv behaviour for two checks in the base's own attribute loop: WGL_CONTEXT_OPENGL_NO_ERROR_ARB is accepted and ignored, and 3.2-4.1 core requests no longer need the forward-compatible flag. Not taken: upstream's handling of legacy versions (3.0 without flags, 3.1, and 1.x/2.x with the forward-compatible bit, which upstream accepts), of an explicit zero profile mask (upstream defaults it to core), of 3.2+ compatibility profiles, and its ERROR_INVALID_VERSION_ARB for a 3.2-4.1 request above the host maximum (the base returns ERROR_INVALID_PROFILE_ARB). Those requests keep their base results.
patches.summary: Let winemac.drv create OpenGL 3.2-4.1 core contexts requested with WGL_CONTEXT_OPENGL_NO_ERROR_ARB and without the forward-compatible flag, as SDL 2 requests them, instead of failing (ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER for the no-error attribute, ERROR_INVALID_VERSION_ARB without the forward-compatible flag). A program that probed for a core context and fell back to a legacy one now gets the core context, as on upstream Wine 11.19.
patches.testStrategy: tests/macdrv-context-attribs-check.py compiles the patched macdrv_context_create() with a stubbed CGL context and CX_FWD_COMPAT_GL_CTX unset: the SDL 2.0.16 3.2 core request (major 3, minor 2, core profile, no-error 0, no flags), a 3.2 core request without no-error, a 2.1 request with no-error 1 and a 4.1 request with no-error 1 succeed, and the 3.2 request still succeeds with CX_FWD_COMPAT_GL_CTX=1; a 3.2 compatibility profile, 3.0 and 3.1 requests, a 4.3 request, an unknown attribute and a forward-compatible 2.1 request are refused with their previous errors. Reverting either half fails it. scripts/integration-check.sh runs it for patch sets carrying this patch. It does not cover CGL context creation; a complete WoW64 build and an application run are still required before tagging.

patches.summary: Adds a mesagl backend id to the per-process graphics route table: a process whose own image is inside a routed directory gets RUNEON_GFX_DIR_MESAGL prepended to its builtin search path, so a builtin-marked Mesa opengl32 resolves there, as does any helper module for which a launcher provides a prefix placeholder. Direct3D modules stay with plain Wine, whose wined3d then also uses that opengl32, so the route suits OpenGL-only applications. Without the variable and without a mesagl table entry behaviour is unchanged; a mesagl route without the variable loads plain Wine.
patches.testStrategy: tests/graphics-route-check.py compiles the patched route parser and, when the mesagl backend is present, checks the mesagl route, malformed ids, overlap, the missing-directory fallback and that the variable alone enables the table. patches.summary: When RUNEON_GFX_DIR_MESAGL is set, winemac.drv reports once per process that a legacy (OpenGL 2.1) context was requested and once that a core context was requested, after the existing checks, so a launcher can attribute a failed start to the legacy context limit. Lines are reported on request, not on success; win32u's internal pbuffer contexts also count as legacy, and requests refused by the checks (for example 3.0/3.1 or compatibility 3.2+) report nothing. Diagnostics only; context creation is unchanged.

patches.summary: kernelbase supports code page 54936 (GB18030), which Windows implements in code and Wine lacks (WineHQ bug 45339): IsValidCodePage(), GetCPInfo(), GetCPInfoExW(), MultiByteToWideChar() and WideCharToMultiByte() accept it, mapped as GB18030-2000. Two-byte codes reuse the code page 936 table with 81 overrides; four-byte codes use 206 BMP ranges and a linear mapping for the supplementary planes. Flags are validated as for UTF-8 so a default MB_PRECOMPOSED is not rejected; invalid input decodes to U+FFFD and lone surrogates to the default character unless the strict flags ask for an error. Other code pages are unchanged.
patches.testStrategy: tests/gb18030-codepage-check.py compiles the patched conversion helpers, with only the surrogate macros include/winnls.h defines, against the tree's nls/c_936.nls and compares every BMP character, supplementary samples and every two-byte code with Python's GB18030-2000 codec in both directions, pins the codes where the 2000 and 2005 editions differ, and covers invalid, truncated and unassigned input, lone surrogates, the strict flags and short buffers in both directions; changing an override, a range, the supplementary base or the replacement character fails it. A complete WoW64 build and an application run are still required before tagging.

verification.contains: static int mbstowcs_gb18030( DWORD flags, const unsigned char *src, int srclen, WCHAR *dst, int dstlen )

patches.summary: msvcrt keeps refusing code page 54936 in setlocale() and _setmbcp(), as it did before 0115 made kernelbase accept it: the CRT's character tables assume at most two bytes per character, and Microsoft documents no multibyte CRT code page beyond two bytes except UTF-8. Programs that fall back to another locale when this fails keep doing so.
